tested_scope: One bounded official-GitHub documentation audit of logical owner/name reuse after repository rename, transfer, and username change, bound to the Part116 moved-repository numeric-id observation.
observations: GitHub's repository rename documentation states that if a new repository later reuses the original repository name, redirects to the renamed repository no longer work.
GitHub's repository transfer documentation states that creating a new repository or fork at the previous repository location permanently deletes redirects to the transferred repository.

GitHub's username-change documentation states that if a new owner claims the old username and creates a repository with the same name, that repository overrides the redirect and the old redirect stops working.
inference: Logical owner/name paths are not incarnation-safe authority identifiers across reuse. A stale claimant bound only to an old logical path can be redirected during one interval and later resolve to a distinct repository incarnation after path reuse; therefore path identity must not be treated as a permanent claim/fencing identity.
binding_to_part116: Part116 observed numeric repository-id continuity for one historical moved repository. Part117 narrows the claim: the logical path is explicitly reusable/redirect-invalidatable, but the official documentation audited here does not establish global non-reuse or delete/recreate lifecycle guarantees for numeric repository id or node_id. Canonical /repositories/{id} plus node_id therefore remains only a candidate identity within tested/documented lifecycle scope, not an accepted permanent incarnation token.
source_qualification: Official GitHub Docs: Renaming a repository (Enterprise Cloud latest), warning that reusing the original name stops redirects.
Official GitHub Docs: Transferring a repository, warning that a new repository or fork at the previous location permanently deletes redirects.
Official GitHub Docs: Username changes, explaining that a new owner creating the same repository name overrides the redirect.

phase1_result.new_falsification: owner/name is not incarnation-safe across rename/transfer/username-path reuse
phase1_result.minimal_unresolved_child: Audit official GitHub guarantees, if any, for repository numeric id and node_id uniqueness/non-reuse across deletion, restoration, transfer and recreation; if no durable non-reuse guarantee exists, test a repository-local monotonic incarnation record guarded by current-blob CAS as the next zero-cost claim identity candidate.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.repository_transport_note: Only lightweight repository state/evidence transport is used; API availability/rate limits remain a checkpoint/retry concern and are not treated as compute or correctness authority.
